Exact-interface follow-up — Solstice LNF oil pan

Access/research date: 2026-10-13. Research-only addition; P2 geometry, delivery worksheet, original sources and historical research remain unchanged. Inputs read: STATUS.md, QUALITY.md, research/oil-pan-evidence.md, and all 29 rows of delivery/MEASUREMENTS_REQUIRED.csv.

Result

The pass adds a Solstice LNF catalog fastener identification and original GM exploded-view topology, but no measured hidden-cavity dimension, five-boss coordinate, seating height, usable thread depth or pickup keepout envelope. The actual-interface worksheet rows remain UNKNOWN. P2's approximately 160 × 120 × 47.2192 mm assembly envelope remains a design assumption. The older research note's 35 mm enclosure proposal is historical and is not the current dimensional authority.

Original catalog illustration: solstice-lnf-epc.png. It was visually inspected. Exploded distances and drawn lengths are schematic, not dimensions. The illustration separates the cover, routed suction tube/screen and pipe bolt; it does not expose a dimensioned internal boss/floor section.

The 2009 Saturn Sky catalog, accessed 2026-10-13 through web text, lists the same 11519133 description with quantity 05, alongside 12601240 and 12578196. This supports the five-screw interpretation already visible in the OEM cover image, but is a dealer catalog and sibling application. The inspected 2008 Solstice GMPartsGiant list did not expose 11519133; that omission is not treated as contradictory hardware evidence.

Official GM cross-check and its limits

GM official 11519133 product, accessed 2026-10-13, confirms this GM bolt identity. Its generic application description concerns four bolts on LS-series engines. That text does not identify Solstice application or baffle quantity. Solstice linkage comes from the reproduced EPC above, with official GM corroborating the part identity only.

One web extraction of the official page exposed a 13.2 mm thread-length attribute; a later open returned only classification. The EPC instead explicitly labels 13.2 OD. Preserve this attribute discrepancy; neither value is adopted as usable engagement. The unmodified official bolt photograph was downloaded and inspected as gm-11519133-primary.jpg. It has no dimensional scale and cannot resolve the discrepancy or installed thread condition.

The already captured official GM 12601240 product publishes 474.7 × 316 × 117.99 mm overall envelope. That establishes neither sump floor-to-cover spacing nor a rectangular internal cavity. The existing GM cover/interior photos provide topology, not exact mounting dimensions. Ambiguous reseller “item dimensions” are not promoted.

Service evidence and changed stack

The 2008 Solstice L4-2.0L Turbo cleaning/inspection procedure reproduced by CHARM was rechecked through indexed web text on 2026-10-13. It keeps the press-fit screen in the pan, removes/reinstalls the baffle, and specifies 14 N·m for the original baffle bolts. Direct page retrieval again failed; no service-image original was recovered in this pass.

That original torque does not establish a modified clamp stack's seating, preload, engagement, fatigue strength or thread-form compatibility. Nominal M6×1×20 screw identification also does not establish usable hole depth. Inserting straps under the original cover or bolt changes stack/cover position and can reduce engagement or create unwanted contact. These are still measured-design questions. The catalog's separate pipe bolt does not contradict the instruction to leave the press-fit screen alone; screen retention and pipe fastening are distinct features.

Datum implications for the measurement sheet

  • The two cataloged pan locating dowels could help relate a removed pan to its block mating datum, once identified and measured. Their published size supplies no position, coplanarity or internal-cover-seat relationship.
  • The five baffle seating pads must each be measured; neither the illustration nor the loose plate image proves they are coplanar.
  • Use a documented common datum for cover seats, pickup and floor sections. Register this to actual installed car axes/tilt separately. Catalog engine orientation is illustrative.
  • The newly identified screw narrows the identification task. It closes no worksheet row that requires actual identity, measured thread depth, original stack or saved uncertainty.

What this pass can change

The next physical identification can check 11519133 / M6×1×20 self-tapping baffle screws, the separate pipe attachment, and two 8×12 mm locating dowels instead of starting with generic assumptions. The current cover-retaining concept remains conditional. No evidence in this pass supports reducing a clearance allowance, fixing the mounting blank locations, selecting a longer replacement screw, or treating the P2 cage envelope as fitted.
